Class CursorWindow

java.lang.Object
io.micronaut.data.nitrite.runtime.read.CursorWindow
@Internal public final class CursorWindow extends Object
Bounds how many documents a cursor yields, for a read whose bound should not be given to Nitrite.

For MVStore and in-memory storage, a find that carries a row bound and a sort is ordered from an index on the sort field rather than blocking-sorted. That path measured about 3.4 times slower than the blocking sort on every collection size and bound tried, at a cost that grows with the collection rather than with the bound, so a sorted read is issued unbounded and bounded here instead. RocksDB is an exception: its bounded indexed path is faster in the benchmark, so its bound remains on the find. A skip is unaffected and stays with the find, which makes the cursor window only ever drop a suffix of the cursor.

Since:
5.2.0

    • withholdSortedLimit

      public static long withholdSortedLimit(org.dizitart.no2.collection.FindOptions options, boolean useCursorLimit)
      Takes the row bound off a sorted find when the backend benefits from cursor-side limiting.
      Parameters:
      options - the find options, whose bound is cleared when the find is sorted
      useCursorLimit - whether to move a sorted bound from the find to the cursor
      Returns:
      the withheld bound, or -1 when the find should retain its bound
